e569-e2e-harness.note: ISSUE #569. RAI RULED DIRECTLY (2026-08-28): upgrade Playwright AND Electron to the latest MUTUALLY-COMPATIBLE versions — NOT a minimal pin-back, NOT a workaround, and NOT amending C14's packet around it. Fix the harness properly. Current break: 'Electron: bad option: --remote-debugging-port=0', Electron 43.2.0 vs @playwright/test 1.62.0, failing at electron.launch BEFORE any app code runs — so it blocks EVERY Electron spec identically, including the four pre-existing ones. Pre-existing and repo-wide (controlled: an untouched spec on main fails identically), NOT caused by c20. LATEST COMPATIBLE, NOT LATEST INDEPENDENTLY — picking each side's newest in isolation is exactly how 43.2.0 met 1.62.0. If they cannot both be latest, take the newest compatible PAIR and report the constraint; never silently pick one side. Dependency standard + npmrc min-release-age=7 planned around, NOT overridden. ACCEPTANCE BAR: the four pre-existing desktop E2E specs actually RUN AND PASS (not merely that electron.launch stops erroring), plus rennet-desktop:package-smoke, plus full pnpm check with a GATE_EXIT line. c20's corner-slot spec runs as an informational fifth — its verdict is c20's business. Electron majors move Chromium, so app-level breakage (renderer APIs, daemon supervisor, apps/desktop/src/main) is IN SCOPE to fix: an upgrade that green-lights E2E while breaking the app is worse than the status quo. *** SEQUENCING PRIORITY: this is worth MORE THAN ITS OWN SCOPE. A working harness is the ONLY thing that would smoke-test the release before it auto-updates onto Rai's machine — right now NOTHING does. So it lands ahead of c21 session-mint if a choice is forced: a broken release reaching him is worse than a late one. Footprint (package.json + lockfile + apps/desktop) collides with c20, so it folds c20's main and lands AFTER c20 — implementation runs in parallel, landing serializes. Must land BEFORE the release and obviously before C14. *** Converted in-flight from a timeboxed spike; timebox lifted. ONE agent on these files. | *** FIXED @de61a1ce (GATE_EXIT=0, package-smoke PASS) — AND THE DIAGNOSIS OVERTURNED OUR WHOLE THEORY. IT WAS NEVER A VERSION MISMATCH. ROOT CAUSE: ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 is exported into every shell whose parent is itself an Electron app — INCLUDING THE AGENT TERMINAL THIS BUILD RUNS IN. Both apps/desktop/e2e/harness.ts and scripts/smoke-packaged-app.mjs spread process.env into the launch, so the Electron binary ran as BARE NODE and Playwright's --remote-debugging-port hit NODE'S option parser. Bisected on the SAME electron 43 / playwright 1.62 pair: var set -> 'bad option'; env -u -> 'DevTools listening'. Fix is `delete environment.ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE` in two files. Rennet's own daemon spawn sets the var explicitly, so dropping the INHERITED value costs nothing. LESSON FOR THE RECORD: the version-incompatibility theory (mine and the coordinator's) was WRONG, and it would have STAYED wrong if the agent had bumped versions and declared victory when the symptom moved. A symptom moving is not a cause found. It honoured Rai's ruling anyway: playwright 1.62.1 + electron 43.4.1, the newest ELIGIBLE pair (electron 44.0.0 is 3 days old, excluded under min-release-age=7), dependency-standard table updated. *** SETUP NOTE: it ran `playwright install chromium` locally (machine-level, was absent) — capture in CI/setup docs or the next machine hits it. LANDS AFTER c20 (footprint collision on apps/desktop).
